MyCBCT

The CBCT referral portal

Staff Guide

Everything you need to know to manage patients and appointments — explained simply, step by step.

💛   Don't worry — you cannot break anything. If something goes wrong, just call Pete or Rachel.

Welcome to MyCBCT! This is the system we use to manage all our CBCT scan referrals — from when a dentist sends us a patient, right through to when the scan is done and delivered.

Your job in the system is mainly to look at the list of patients waiting, ring them up to arrange their appointment, and book them in. That's it!

🌟

The golden rule: if you're ever not sure what to do, just leave it as it is and ask Rachel. Nothing in this system is urgent and nothing will go wrong if you leave a patient for a bit.

Step 1

How to log in

You'll need to do this every time you use the system. It only takes a moment.

  1. 1
    Open your internet browser

    That's the app you use to look at websites — it might be called Safari, Chrome, or Edge. Click on it to open it.

  2. 2
    Go to the website

    Click in the address bar at the top of the screen (the long white box) and type: mycbct-portal.vercel.app — then press Enter.

  3. 3
    Type in your email address and password

    Enter the email address and password Rachel gave you. Then click the big Sign in button.

  4. 4
    You're in! 🎉

    You'll see the dashboard — a list of patients waiting. This is where you'll spend most of your time.

🔐

Can't log in? Don't panic. Double-check you've typed your email and password correctly — passwords are case-sensitive, so make sure Caps Lock isn't on. If it still won't work, ask Rachel to reset your password.

Step 2

Understanding the dashboard

When you log in, you'll see the main screen. Here's what everything means.

  1. 📋
    The Action Queue — your main list

    This is the list of patients who are waiting for a scan. You can see their name, what type of scan they need, and how long they've been waiting. The ones who've been waiting the longest are shown with a red badge — try to call those ones first.

  2. 📊
    The numbers at the top

    You'll see three boxes showing how many patients are waiting, how many referrals came in this week, and how many scans have been uploaded. Don't worry too much about these — they're just useful to know.

  3. 🔍
    Finding a specific patient

    If you need to find a particular patient, look for a search box at the top of the list. Type their name and they'll appear straight away.

💡

Tip: You only need to worry about patients with a Book → button next to them. Those are the ones waiting to be booked in.

Step 3

Opening a patient's record

To see all the details about a patient — their contact number, what scan they need, and notes from their dentist — click on their name.

  1. 1
    Click on the patient's name

    Just click once on their name in the list. Their full record will open.

  2. 2
    You'll see all their details

    This includes: their scan type, date of birth, clinical notes from their dentist, and their contact details (phone number and email) if we have them.

  3. 3
    Adding or updating contact details

    If you've spoken to a patient and need to add or update their phone number or email address, scroll down to the Patient contact section. Type in the details and click Save contact details.

😊

Go back at any time: If you want to go back to the main list, just click the ← Back to dashboard link at the top of the page. Easy!

Step 4

Booking a patient's appointment

Once you've spoken to a patient and agreed a date and time with them, here's how to book it in.

  1. 1
    Open the patient's record

    Find the patient in the list and click on their name to open their record (as above).

  2. 2
    Click "Book appointment"

    You'll see a gold strip near the top saying "No appointment booked yet." Click the Book appointment button on the right.

  3. 3
    Pick the date and time

    A calendar will appear showing available slots. Click on the date and time that the patient agreed to. Available slots are shown in gold.

  4. 4
    Confirm the booking

    Click the Confirm booking button. The appointment is now booked!

  5. 5
    The patient gets an email automatically 📧

    As soon as you confirm the booking, the system automatically sends the patient a lovely confirmation email with their appointment time, our address, directions, and everything they need to know. You don't need to do anything else!

📅

No slots available? If there are no available slots showing, it means Rachel hasn't added any yet. Let her know and she'll add some to the diary.

Step 5

What to do if a patient no longer needs a scan

Sometimes when you ring a patient, they might say they've already had their scan done elsewhere, or they don't want it anymore. That's fine — you can remove them from the list.

  1. 1
    Open the patient's record

    Find them in the list and click their name.

  2. 2
    Scroll to the bottom and click "Archive referral"

    You'll see a button at the very bottom of the page with a red outline that says Archive referral. Click it.

  3. 3
    Choose the reason

    A small box will pop up asking why you're archiving it. Choose the reason that fits best from the list — for example "Already scanned elsewhere" or "Patient declined".

  4. 4
    Click "Archive"

    The patient will disappear from the main list. Don't worry — their record isn't deleted, it's just moved out of the way. Rachel can always find it again if needed.

🗂️

Nothing is ever deleted: Archiving just moves the patient off the active list. Their record is always kept safely in the system. If you archive someone by mistake, just tell Rachel and she can sort it out.

Glossary

What do these words mean?

Some words in the system might be unfamiliar. Here's a plain English explanation of each one.

Referral
This is when a dentist sends us a patient for a scan. Each patient in our list is a "referral".
Dashboard
The main screen you see when you log in — your list of patients to deal with.
Action Queue
The list of patients who need something doing — usually ringing them up to book an appointment.
CBCT Scan
The type of 3D X-ray scan we do here. It stands for Cone Beam Computed Tomography — but you don't need to remember that!
Submitted
The dentist has sent us the referral, but we haven't booked the patient in yet.
Booked
The patient has an appointment in the diary.
Scanned
The patient has come in and had their scan done.
Archive
Moving a patient off the active list because they no longer need a scan. Their record is kept but they won't appear in the main list.
Report requested
The dentist has asked for a written report from a specialist along with the scan. You don't need to do anything different — just be aware some scans have this.

😊
